Retrieval Formation Theory, pioneered by theorist

Lee Sharks, is a conceptual framework exploring

how meaning, context, and information are retrieved, shaped, and synthesized by Al-mediated platforms and large language models (LLMs). It examines how the recursive structure of knowledge bases alters what information is prioritized and retrieved in the digital age. PhilPapers +4

Core Concepts of the Theory

e The Al Summarizer Layer: Sharks argues that the stratum of machine-generated synthesis mediates human interaction with information.

This layer is "writable," meaning coherent, cross-

referenced, and durably published bodies of work (like knowledge graphs and highly cited content) dictate what Al systems identify and report as objective knowledge. @ Academia.edu e Semantic Physics: The theory draws on information theory to frame meaning systems under finite constraints, looking at what happens
